facts.fact: By the time Carson had showered and changed, Meme already had dinner waiting — roast chicken, mashed potatoes, green beans and an apple pie — even though there were only two of them.
facts.anchor: Tonight, that meant roast chicken, mashed potatoes, green beans, and an apple pie cooling on the counter despite there only being two of us.

facts.fact: Meme made vanilla pudding to go with the pie because Pops had always insisted the two belonged together, and Pops had done it for more than forty years while Meme never stopped making it.
facts.anchor: but Pops had done it for more than forty years, and Meme had never stopped making it.

facts.fact: Carson observed that her grandmother Meme (Evelyn Rome) was seventy-three yet still wore pink lip gloss at nearly eight at night, even after spending the morning feeding calves.
facts.anchor: Evelyn Rome was seventy-three and somehow still prettier than most women half her age.

facts.fact: At seventeen, Carson had spent more weekends outside Willow Creek while she and Pops chased every event they could reach because sponsors were beginning to notice her.
facts.anchor: At seventeen, I’d spent more weekends outside Willow Creek than inside it.

facts.fact: Meme told Carson she had walked more than two miles in soaking wet jeans and reminded her that moisture around the socket causes problems.
facts.anchor: You walked more than two miles in soaking wet jeans.

facts.fact: During the phone call, Beau told Carson he would rather not see her wait more than a month before getting the brakes done.
facts.anchor: Brakes? I’d rather not see you wait more than a month.

facts.fact: By six, Carson had fed Blueberry, checked the calves, helped move two cows into the milking parlor, and listened to Earl complain for twelve minutes about a gate hinge he had been telling her to replace since July.
facts.anchor: By six, I’d fed Blueberry, checked the calves, helped move two cows into the milking parlor, discovered another section of fencing that needed repairing, and listened to Earl complain for twelve minutes about a gate hinge he’d been telling me to replace since July.

facts.fact: By seven thirty, Carson sat at Pops’s old desk in the ranch office with three different bills — feed, electricity, mortgage — spread across the wood.
facts.anchor: By seven thirty, I was sitting at Pops’s old desk in the ranch office with coffee going cold beside me and three different bills spread across the wood.
